key_sections.Section 9: Courts to try all civil suits unless expressly or impliedly barred.
key_sections.Section 10: Stay of suit (Res Sub-Judice) where matter directly in issue in previously instituted suit.
key_sections.Section 11: Res Judicata and Constructive Res Judicata (Explanation IV).
key_sections.Section 16: Suits to be instituted where subject-matter property is situated.
key_sections.Section 20: Other suits to be instituted where defendants reside or cause of action arises.
key_sections.Section 26: Institution of suits by presentation of plaint.
key_sections.Section 34: Interest pre-suit, pendente lite, and future post-decree up to 6% or commercial contractual rate.
key_sections.Section 80: Mandatory 2-month prior notice to Government or Public Officer before institution.
key_sections.Section 89: Alternative Dispute Resolution (Arbitration, Conciliation, Lok Adalat, Mediation).
key_sections.Section 151: Inherent powers of the Court to prevent abuse of process and secure ends of justice.

key_orders.Order II Rule 2: Suit to include whole claim; omission to sue for one of several reliefs without leave bars subsequent suit.
key_orders.Order VI Rule 15A: Mandatory Statement of Truth for Commercial Suits (Commercial Courts Act, 2015).
key_orders.Order VII Rule 11: Mandatory Rejection of Plaint (11a: no cause of action, 11b: undervaluation, 11c: deficit court fee, 11d: barred by law/limitation).
key_orders.Order VIII Rule 1: Written Statement timeline: 30 days basic, 90 days max for ordinary suits, strictly 120 days mandatory forfeiture for Commercial Suits.
key_orders.Order XIII-A: Summary Judgment in Commercial Disputes (no real prospect of succeeding/defending).
key_orders.Order XXI Rule 11: Execution of Decrees and Orders; Garnishee proceedings u/O XXI R 46A-46I.
key_orders.Order XXXVII: Summary Procedure on Bills of Exchange, Hundies, Promissory Notes, and written liquidated debt guarantees.
key_orders.Order XXXVIII Rule 5: Attachment Before Judgment upon strict proof of intent to obstruct execution.
key_orders.Order XXXIX Rule 1 & 2: Temporary Injunction 3-Prong Golden Triad: Prima Facie Case, Balance of Convenience, Irreparable Injury.

COMMERCIAL_COURTS_ACT_2015.title: Commercial Courts Act, 2015
COMMERCIAL_COURTS_ACT_2015.Section 2(1)(c): 22 distinct categories of commercial transactions and disputes.
COMMERCIAL_COURTS_ACT_2015.Section 12A: Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement (PIMS) mandatory condition precedent unless urgent interim relief is sought.

SPECIFIC_RELIEF_ACT_1963.title: Specific Relief Act, 1963 (as amended by 2018 Amendment)
SPECIFIC_RELIEF_ACT_1963.Section 10: Mandatory Specific Performance of Contracts (discretionary power removed).
SPECIFIC_RELIEF_ACT_1963.Section 16(c): Continuous readiness and willingness of plaintiff from agreement date to decree.
SPECIFIC_RELIEF_ACT_1963.Section 20: Substituted Performance of contract after 30 days notice to defaulting party.
SPECIFIC_RELIEF_ACT_1963.Section 20A: Absolute statutory bar on granting injunctions that impede or delay Infrastructure Projects.
SPECIFIC_RELIEF_ACT_1963.Section 34: Discretion of court as to declaration of legal character or right.

LIMITATION_ACT_1963.title: Limitation Act, 1963
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Section 3: Mandatory dismissal of suits instituted after prescribed period of limitation.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Section 18: Effect of written acknowledgment of liability in writing (restarts 3-year limitation).
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Section 19: Effect of payment on account of debt or interest (restarts limitation).
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 14: Price of goods sold and delivered: 3 years from date of delivery.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 22: Money deposited payable on demand: 3 years from date of demand.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 54: Specific performance of contract: 3 years from date fixed for performance, or date of notice of refusal.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 55: Compensation for breach of contract: 3 years from date contract is broken.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 58: Suit for declaration: 3 years from date when right to sue first accrues.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 65: Possession of immovable property based on title: 12 years when possession becomes adverse.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 113: Residuary limitation for civil suits: 3 years from accrual of right to sue.
LIMITATION_ACT_1963.Article 136: Execution of decree or order: 12 years from when decree becomes enforceable.

patil_automation.citation: Patil Automation Pvt Ltd v. Rakheja Engineers Pvt Ltd (2022) 10 SCC 1
patil_automation.ratio: Section 12A Pre-Institution Mediation is mandatory in commercial suits. Plaints filed without PIMS and without praying for urgent interim relief must be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 CPC.

scg_contracts.citation: SCG Contracts (India) Pvt Ltd v. K.S. Chamankar Infrastructure (2019) 12 SCC 210
scg_contracts.ratio: The 120-day outer limit for filing Written Statement in Commercial Suits under Order VIII Rule 1 proviso is mandatory; right to file WS stands irrevocably forfeited after 120 days.

dahiben.citation: Dahiben v. Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali (2020) 7 SCC 366
dahiben.ratio: Order VII Rule 11(d) mandates rejection of plaint if clear reading of plaint demonstrates suit is barred by limitation or is an illusion of cause of action.

virgo_industries.citation: Virgo Industries (Eng.) Pvt Ltd v. Venturetech Solutions Pvt Ltd (2013) 1 SCC 625
virgo_industries.ratio: Order II Rule 2 CPC bars a subsequent suit for specific performance if the plaintiff earlier filed a suit for injunction on the same cause of action without seeking leave of court.

dalpat_kumar.citation: Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh (1992) 1 SCC 719
dalpat_kumar.ratio: Temporary injunction under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 requires conclusive satisfaction of three co-existing conditions: Prima Facie Case, Balance of Convenience, and Irreparable Injury.

wander_ltd.citation: Wander Ltd v. Antox India Pvt Ltd (1990) Supp SCC 727
wander_ltd.ratio: In balance of convenience analysis, court must balance comparative hardship to parties pending final adjudication.

hubtown.citation: IDBI Trusteeship Services Ltd v. Hubtown Ltd (2017) 1 SCC 568
hubtown.ratio: Principles for Leave to Defend: Substantial defense warrants unconditional leave; triable issue with doubt warrants conditional leave with deposit; sham defense warrants refusal of leave and immediate decree.

un_krishnamurthy.citation: U.N. Krishnamurthy v. A.M. Krishnamurthy (2022) SCC OnLine SC 840
un_krishnamurthy.ratio: Section 16(c) Specific Relief Act mandates continuous readiness and willingness. Plaintiff must produce documentary proof of financial capacity (bank balance, deposits, or credit availability) at date of breach.

kailash_nath.citation: Kailash Nath Associates v. Delhi Development Authority (2015) 4 SCC 136
kailash_nath.ratio: Under Section 74 Indian Contract Act, liquidated damages named in contract represent upper limit; party claiming compensation must prove actual loss unless impossible to assess.

booz_allen.citation: Booz Allen & Hamilton Inc v. SBI Home Finance Ltd (2011) 5 SCC 532
booz_allen.ratio: Where arbitration agreement exists, Section 8 mandates court to refer parties to arbitration upon application filed before submitting first statement on substance of dispute.

rahul_s_shah.citation: Rahul S. Shah v. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi (2021) 6 SCC 418
rahul_s_shah.ratio: Executing courts must dispose of execution petitions within 6 months and mandate judgment debtors to file affidavits of assets under Order XXI Rule 41 CPC.

raman_tech.citation: Raman Tech & Process Engg Co v. Quality Buildcon Pvt Ltd (2008) 2 SCC 302
raman_tech.ratio: Power under Order XXXVIII Rule 5 is drastic and cannot be exercised routinely to convert unsecured debt into secured debt; clear prima facie proof of intent to obstruct execution required.
